setter.evidence: No setter named. The prospect says his partner made first contact: 'was my girlfriend that got in touch with you guys'.

prospect.name: Bruno
prospect.location: Australia — living there but not an Australian resident, so paying for all treatment privately
prospect.occupation: Pickleball coach, formerly a tennis coach; barely working at present — 'I got back to work yesterday actually, but I'm working just a little bit, just doing a few private lessons here and there'
prospect.family_status: Lives with his girlfriend in a two-bedroom apartment; she manages the household finances and made first contact with the company
prospect.training_background: Lifelong athlete and racquet-sports coach; played roughly 12 hours over three days the previous weekend. Trains with strength conditioning at least three times a week, up from once or twice before the diagnosis. Already owns a kettlebell, has swung 25 kg, and used to travel with one.
prospect.medical: Aggressive malignant brain tumour. Presented with a seizure, CT found the tumour, had brain surgery about eight weeks ago and a biopsy confirming an aggressive cancer he describes as 'the third worst brain cancer that you can have' with a quoted prognosis of 'three to five years of life'. Currently at session 18 of 33 daily radiotherapy sessions, five days a week, with roughly three weeks left; then a four-week break, then twelve months of chemotherapy. Energy at about 75%; head 'still healing'; sleeping more. Stiff back and hips, weak shoulders and wrists, and possible new back injury from the weekend, unassessed — 'I'm going to go to the physio, see what's going on'. On a ketogenic diet since surgery. Uses a hyperbaric oxygen chamber and a home sauna daily.

signals: In the middle of a serious active health event, not recovering from one — session 18 of 33 radiotherapy sessions with twelve months of chemotherapy ahead

Training explicitly framed as preparation for treatment: 'I just want to like build a bit of core, a bit of mobility, build a bit of muscles in these next two months that I have to do it before I start chemo because it will be important'
Extremely high motivation, which the rep named on the call: 'I think you have the strongest why you need to do it out of all of the guys that I've ever spoke to over here'
No resistance to the concept at any point — the only blocker raised was cash, because savings are being consumed by private cancer treatment

goals.text: Get his body as strong as possible in the two months before chemotherapy starts, so he can withstand treatment
Build mobility and clear the stiffness in his back and hips
Build some muscle and core strength — explicitly not to lift heavy or get 'extremely stronger'
Keep playing and coaching pickleball right through radiation and chemotherapy
Train at home with a few kettlebells rather than commit to a gym he would not stay motivated to attend
Reduce what his diagnosis is doing to the people around him — 'the main thing... would be like seeing people around suffering with it'

pains.text: Aggressive brain cancer eight weeks post-surgery, mid-radiotherapy, with a year of chemotherapy ahead
Energy down to about 75%, needing extra sleep after each radiotherapy session
Body noticeably weaker since the diagnosis and picking up injuries — 'My body's a bit weaker, so I'm getting a few injuries here and there'
Possible new back injury from playing 12 hours over a weekend, not yet assessed by the physio
Stiff hips and back, weak shoulders and wrists from years of racquet sports with too little strength work
Anxiety about how chemotherapy will hit him — 'now is what I'm anxious about and I don't know how the chemo is going to be'
Savings being drained by privately funded cancer care as a non-resident, with future costs uncertain
Watching the people who love him suffer alongside the diagnosis

objections.raw_quote: Leaning towards the six months. I mean, just a matter of financial-wise, like, I'll watch your pay, and I just need to check with my girlfriend. But yeah, just need to check. If we have the money to do it, we're gonna do it for sure.
objections.rep_response: Ran the money-aside isolation ('money aside, like, do you personally feel that this can get you [there]?'), confirmed the girlfriend was supportive, then asked him to wake her and put her on the call immediately.

objections.raw_quote: I live in Australia, But I'm not Australian resident. So I'm paying everything privately. I'm paying, like, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and those things cost a fortune. So all my savings are going through cancer sheets, and doctors, and blood exams, and MRIs, and supplements.
objections.rep_response: Reframed it as logistics rather than desire, then offered to split the payment but required the prospect to name a starting figure first. No financial picture beyond a vague question about his checking account.

objections.raw_quote: it's hard to commit for, like, big investments when you have something like I do. I wasn't aware of the price at all. don't know, it was, like, thousands and thousands of dollars.
objections.rep_response: Did not address the medical-uncertainty part at all. Answered only the payment-plan request: 'we don't have, like, a set payment plans. We always work around what's, like, in a particular case of each individual.'

objections.raw_quote: we are really keen. We just cannot give you an answer right now because we need to check the finances. That's all.
objections.rep_response: Accepted and booked a call for the following day at 7pm.

offer.payment_plan_terms: None agreed. Rep said only 'there are ways that we can move around with finances. If the payment in one installment is difficult, we can work around and maybe split it. But I would need to know from you what level of investments you can commit to at the beginning', and separately 'we don't have, like, a set payment plans. We always work around what's, like, in a particular case of each individual.' No figures, instalment count or schedule were put on the table.

prospect_financials.note: Has savings but they are being consumed by privately funded cancer treatment. Partner controls the household finances. He would not name a number: 'I just need to check the bills, go through the bills again, and speak to her and see if we have the money to afford the 6,000 USD.'

evidence: Strong verbal agreement to the concept before price: 'Yeah, 100%. That's what I'm looking for. That's for sure. So, let's do it, yeah?' — but this was the commitment check, not agreement to buy
After the number, no agreement: 'We just cannot give you an answer right now because we need to check the finances'
Leaning six months at $6,000 but conditional: 'If we have the money to do it, we're gonna do it for sure'
No payment taken and no payment link sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule does not apply
Follow-up booked for the next day at 7pm his time, invite to be emailed
outcome.next_step: Call the following day at 19:00 the prospect's time, after he and his girlfriend review their bills; he also asked to be sent payment options in writing.

notable.note: The most serious clinical exposure in this batch. The prospect has an aggressive brain tumour, is eight weeks post-craniotomy, is mid-radiotherapy with a seizure as his presenting symptom and a year of chemotherapy ahead, and has an unassessed back injury — and was taken through the full offer and a commitment close for loaded ballistic kettlebell training with no question asked about whether his oncology or surgical team has cleared exercise. The rep also opened with 'everything is going to work out fine', framed the training as preparation for a fight with the cancer, and told him he had 'the strongest why' of any prospect immediately before quoting $9,000.
